label: Where the Views Sit
title: The gifts of the Spirit on one line
intro: Most evangelicals sit somewhere between the two ends rather than in one of three boxes. Each dot is placed by what its own voice says.
image_title: The gifts of the Spirit today: four evangelical views
image_subtitle: From gifts that ceased with the apostles to gifts every believer should seek.
image_subtitle_narrow: From gifts that ceased with the apostles to gifts every believer should seek.
caption: Four views of the miraculous gifts, placed left to right by how much each expects them in the church today. Placement is approximate.

positions.name: Cessationist
positions.text: Apostleship, prophecy, tongues, healing and miracles are no longer regular gifts. God still heals in answer to prayer.
positions.short_text: These gifts are no longer given. God still heals in answer to prayer.

positions.name: Reformed continuationist
positions.text: Every gift continues until Christ returns, tested by Scripture and never equal to it.
positions.short_text: Every gift continues until Christ returns, tested by Scripture.

positions.name: Charismatic evangelical
positions.text: The Spirit gives prophecy, prayer languages, healing and miracles, received without hype.
positions.short_text: Prophecy, prayer languages and healing, without hype.

positions.name: Pentecostal
positions.text: Every believer should seek baptism in the Spirit, first shown by tongues. Healing is provided in the atonement.
positions.short_text: Seek Spirit baptism, first shown by tongues; healing in the atonement.

differ: Whether some gifts stopped when the apostles died, or every gift continues until Christ returns.
What prophecy is today: an impression to be tested (Schreiner), a real gift never equal to Scripture (Storms), or a gift to be weighed carefully and never equal to Scripture (Assemblies of God).
Tongues: likely ended, a gift some receive, a prayer language, or the first sign of baptism in the Spirit.
Healing: all four pray for the sick. They differ on whether healing is still a gift given to some, and whether it is promised in the atonement.
common_text: All four hold Scripture as the final authority over any gift, and all four pray for the sick. Thomas Schreiner, a cessationist, says of the healing God still gives: "we should pray for such."

sources.title: Why I Am a Cessationist
sources.quote: I doubt the gift of miracles and healings exists today
sources.notes: Thomas Schreiner, January 22, 2014. Also on the page: the gifts of apostleship, prophecy, tongues, healing, and miracles are no longer given as a regular feature of church life; what people call prophecy today are impressions that must be tested by Scripture; 'If prophecy has passed away, then tongues have likely ended as well'; 'I believe God still heals and does miraculous things today, and we should pray for such.' The old /article/why-i-am-a-cessationist/ URL redirects here.

sources.title: Why I Am a Continuationist
sources.quote: the burden of proof rests with the cessationist
sources.notes: Sam Storms, January 22, 2014, the companion piece to Schreiner's. Gifts continue until the 'perfect' of 1 Corinthians 13 (Christ's return); 'All the gifts of the Spirit, whether tongues or teaching, prophecy or mercy, healing or helping' build up the church; revelatory gifts do not give 'infallible truths equal in authority to the biblical text itself'; 'I've seen all spiritual gifts in operation, tested and confirmed them'.

sources.title: Core Values and Beliefs
sources.quote: resulting in prophecy, prayer languages, healing, miracles, and many other gifts
sources.notes: PDF linked from vineyardusa.org/about/core-values-beliefs/. Also: 'We eschew hype and other efforts to manipulate either God's presence or the response of others'; healing 'physical, emotional, and social'; the Spirit poured out at Pentecost 'baptizing believers into the Body of Christ and releasing the gifts of the Spirit to them'; Scripture is 'our final, absolute authority'. Vineyard does not use the label Third Wave on these pages, so it is not used here. Its history page: 'We seek to blend the best of the evangelical traditions ... with the best of the Pentecostal and Charismatic traditions'.

sources.title: Statement of Fundamental Truths
sources.quote: witnessed by the initial physical sign of speaking with other tongues as the Spirit of God gives them utterance
sources.notes: Truth 7: all believers 'should ardently expect and earnestly seek' the baptism in the Holy Spirit. Truth 8: tongues as the initial physical sign. Truth 12: 'Divine healing is an integral part of the gospel. Deliverance from sickness is provided for in the atonement'. Truth 1: Scripture is 'the infallible, authoritative rule of faith and conduct'. ag.org returns 403 to scripts; read from the Wayback Machine copy of 2026-11-10.

sources.title: Modern-Day Prophecy (position paper)
sources.quote: No prophecies today carry the authority or weight of Scripture.
sources.notes: Adopted by the General Presbytery, August 4-5, 2025; it replaces the older Apostles and Prophets paper, whose URL now returns an error page. Also: 'Paul called churches to weigh or judge prophecy carefully (1 Corinthians 14:29).' ag.org returns 403 to scripts; read from the Wayback Machine copy of 2026-07-16.
